title: Proxy: mint a Periodical run by registry id (plain or + Autopilot), as the UI does, with an optional operator note
description:
## Goal

An agent holding a proxy token with the `dispatch` grant can mint a Periodical run through the proxy, the way the UI's **Mint** and **Mint + Autopilot** actions do. It needs no checkout of the repo, and the prompt is never rendered on the client.

## Context

`GET /api/proxy/periodicals` reports each template's run state, but nothing in the proxy starts a run. On 5 November an operator session minted three runs:

* Seams & Tangles run 8 (LIN-4298);
* Drift & Coherence run 4 (LIN-4299);
* Comprehension-Debt run 5 (LIN-4300).

It did each one the long way round:

1. **Render the prompt from a checkout:** run the registry's `generatePrompt()` (`lib/periodicals.js`) from a checkout of `main`.
2. **Dispatch it:** post the result to `POST /api/proxy/dispatch` with `kind: "periodical"` and the `periodicalId`.
3. **Start the review by hand:** find the minted ticket and call `/autopilot/kickoff` on it. A proxy-dispatched worker is a leaf and can't enqueue, so the plain mint can't hand off itself.

The prompt text lives server-side in the registry, so the client should never have needed to render it. The UI's "Mint + Autopilot" (`withAutopilotTail`, LIN-1279) already does the hand-off for an owner's dispatch.

## This step

* **A proxy route that mints a Periodical by registry id.**
  * The server renders the registry's own prompt: the plain mint, or the Mint + Autopilot variant when asked.
  * It stamps `periodicalId`, and dispatches as the UI's actions do, with the same grant rules the server already applies to an owner's periodical "+ Autopilot".
  * An unknown id is rejected.
  * Like the other enqueue routes, it requires the `dispatch` grant.
* **An optional short operator note.**
  * The note is bounded in length and carried into the minted task's description above its review contract. That's how the operator's purpose ("this run is also read as …, context not scope") reached the three runs above.
  * The template text itself is never changed.
* **Docs and catalog learn the route:**
  * `docs/proxy-integration.md`;
  * the agent-facing catalog in `lib/proxy-instructions.js`.

  Where the catalog lists periodical ids, derive the list from the registry rather than writing it by hand (Drift run 4, row 131: a hand-written key list in that catalog drifted).

**Not this ticket:** changing any Periodical's prompt, cadence or trigger; scheduling runs; Autopilot's order.

## Done when

* A test shows the route dispatches the same prompt text the UI's action would, for the same id and variant.
* A test shows an unknown id is refused, a token without the `dispatch` grant is refused, and the dispatch appears in `GET /periodicals` run state.
* The docs and the catalog name the route.
* Prompt sizes are unchanged, except for any new catalog text, whose ceiling is raised with its reason recorded.

## How to go about it (from a Survey before work began)

*Pruned at close-out (LIN-4313).* The Survey's conclusion was that the grant was the real work, not the route: the "+ Autopilot" variant needs a declared dispatch grant, so the route got its own owner-checked lane (site `PM`), declared as `LANES.kickoff` is. The full Survey text is preserved in the task snapshots and the comment trail.

## At merge

* The grant test passes: owner allowed with a declared grant, non-owner refused.
* One renderer is used by both callers.
* The parity test passes without a note.
* The note is placed before the template.
* The entrance lists are updated.
* `GET /periodicals` shows the run.

**Decided (John, 6 Nov \~08:50 UTC):** the "+ Autopilot" grant in step 1 is approved, owner-checked as `LANES.kickoff` is. No veto, so the route ships both variants.

## Implementation Plan

*Pruned at close-out (LIN-4313).* Implemented as approved in [https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2324](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2324>) (squash-merged as `c491eca5`): a `LANES.periodical` lane (site `PM`, not the planned next-free tag, because `M3`/`M5` were already taken), `enterPeriodicalMint`, `POST /api/proxy/periodicals/:id/mint`, one shared `renderPeriodicalPrompt`, `ROW_KEYS.periodical`, the free-tier run gate, the note (before the template text), the docs and catalog, and the entrance lists. The plan's section-by-section text (behaviour, places, order, witnesses, risks) is preserved in the task snapshots and the comment trail.

### Size and review

**fits one session.**

plan-review due: yes (it declares a `dispatch` grant on a new door to an orchestrator, and the lane widens what a proxy token can start).

comments.body:
## Survey open-0: LIN-4313 @ 165c61e7f

Read at `165c61e7f` (LinearViewer `origin/main`), task text only.

### Why it's hard

**1. The grant is the real work, not the route.** Mint + Autopilot works only because the session lane *declares* a dispatch grant. `declaresDispatchGrant` (`lib/dispatch-entrance.js:1185`) checks for `kind:'periodical'`, a valid `periodicalId` and `PERIODICAL_AUTOPILOT_TAIL`, but only on `LANES.session` (site `M2`). `LANES.proxy` has `declaration: null`, and `:782` says "the proxy dispatch arms stay undeclared (open question 1)". If the route reuses `enterProxyDispatch`, the variant mints a leaf. The tail's kickoff call then fails, which is the manual step 3 again. The route needs a lane declared like `LANES.kickoff` (`M1`, `grantOwnerAccountId: req.proxyCreatedBy`, owner-checked). That answers open question 1 for this case, an authority decision the ticket only calls "the same rules".

**2. "Same prompt as the UI" has two seams.** The UI adds proxy context only when +proxy is on or forced. The proxy lane adds it by default. Compare the text *before* that block is added, and force the block for the variant, because the tail tells the agent to use its proxy access block. Also, the route must not rebuild `withAutopilotTail(generatePrompt())` itself. Take the rendering out of `buildPeriodicalNodes()` into one function that both the UI and the route call, or the parity test checks a copy of the code.

**3. The note conflicts with parity.** The minted description is written by the Stage-1 agent, and its first line must be the gate marker. So the server can't stamp the note in. It can only tell the agent where to put it, which relies on the model. Parity therefore holds only with no note. The note must sit outside the template without breaking the tail `includes` check, and it needs a length cap and control-character rules, since it is caller text going into a prompt.

**4. Smaller points.**
- `GET /periodicals` counts a queued row as `recent`, so that test is cheap. Stamp `periodicalId`, not just the title.
- The proxy lane defaults the harness to claude-code and the UI path doesn't.
- I found no catalog ceiling, and no periodical-prompt ceiling, in `prompt-size-budget.test.js`. "Raise its ceiling" may mean adding one. A byte-identity test is what actually keeps the prompts unchanged.
- The catalog shows periodical ids only as examples (`proxy-instructions.js:455,834,854`). Derive the list from `getPeriodicals()`, as LIN-4302 proposes for template keys.

### First move

Settle the grant before writing the route. Write a failing test: an owner's `dispatch` token mints the Autopilot variant and the row carries a declared grant, and a non-owner token is refused rather than given a leaf. Then take out the shared prompt renderer. After that, the route is plumbing.

## Survey global: LIN-4313 @ 165c61e7f

**Where it lands.** There are three places. The first is `lib/dispatch-entrance.js`, which was rebuilt design-first in LIN-3604/3611 and is improving. It is now one authority over "four POST handlers", and the ways those handlers differ are written as `LANES` data, each with its reason. The second is `lib/periodicals.js`, the registry where the autopilot tail lives in one place. The third is the hand-kept API prose: `lib/proxy-instructions.js` (1254 lines) and `docs/proxy-integration.md` (2856 lines). These two are growing, and they repeat each other paragraph for paragraph (compare the `periodicalId` text at catalog :834 and docs :2359).

**The obvious way has a hole, and it is the ticket's real subject.** The obvious build is a route that renders `generatePrompt()` or `withAutopilotTail()` and forwards into `enterProxyDispatch`. For the + Autopilot variant, that rebuilds the 5 November failure. The proxy lane has `declaration: null` ("the proxy dispatch arms stay undeclared (open question 1)", dispatch-entrance.js ~:782). The rule that grants a "+ Autopilot" mint the dispatch grant, `declaresDispatchGrant` (:1185, M2b), runs only in the session lane. So the worker would be a grant-less leaf, and its prompt would tell it to `POST /autopilot/kickoff`, which fails. Applying "the same grant rules" means a new declared lane value, as kickoff does (`LANES.kickoff`, M1, which names the token's owner). That makes this route a **fifth entrance**. The things that list the entrances then go stale: the file header ("Four POST handlers"), `tests/unit/dispatch-entrance-pins.test.js`, and `tests/unit/proxy-endpoint-inventory-witness.test.js` (76 hand-listed forms). Since LIN-2505 nothing walks `router.stack`, so **nothing would notice** an unlisted route.

**A second copy waiting to happen.** "Plain prompt, plus tail for the variant" is worked out today only inside `buildPeriodicalNodes` (:1124). A route that calls `generatePrompt()` and `withAutopilotTail()` on its own makes a second copy, and the "same text as the UI" test would then compare two copies rather than one source. The M2b check is also `prompt.includes(PERIODICAL_AUTOPILOT_TAIL)`, so a note placed inside or after the tail could silently drop the grant.

**The note.** The server never writes the minted task. Only the Stage-1 agent does. So "carried into the description above its review contract" can only be done through prompt text the server adds, telling the agent where to put the note. That prompt is then no longer byte-identical to the UI's when a note is present, so the "same text" test should be run without a note.

**Sizes.** No ceiling covers `lib/proxy-instructions.js` or the periodical prompts in `prompt-size-budget.test.js`, and `proxy-instructions.test.js` has no byte check. "Raise its ceiling" has nothing to raise. Either add a ceiling or say plainly that there isn't one. The catalog has no hand-written list of periodical ids today, only the example `documentation-review`. Deriving the list means the catalog imports the registry, which is a new dependency for that file.

**The run-state read already works.** `GET /periodicals` keeps rows where `kind === 'periodical' || periodicalId != null` (proxy-compute.js :1018). Stamping `periodicalId` is enough for the run to show up there.

**Better, at a cost this task can carry:**
- Add one `renderPeriodicalPrompt(id, { autopilot })` to `periodicals.js`, and have both `buildPeriodicalNodes` and the route use it.
- Write the grant declaration as a named lane value with its reason, not as an inline branch.
- Put the note before the template text, so the tail check is untouched.
- Add the route's row to the inventory witness, and update the entrance header and pins.

**Better still, but not this task's to carry:**
- Close "open question 1" for proxy dispatch as a whole, so a leaf's ability to enqueue is decided once.
- Give the catalog a byte ceiling.
- Make one document the source for the catalog and the docs, so the API prose stops being written twice.

### Plan Review Verdict

**Verdict:** Approve — the premise holds at HEAD, the plan covers every item in Done-when, and the grant is owner-checked and refused before anything is enqueued. Six notes below for the builder.

**What I checked** (LinearViewer `main` = `165c61e7`. No commit has touched the plan's files since the ticket was written.)
- **The premise holds.** `LANES.proxy.declaration` is `null` (`lib/dispatch-entrance.js:828`). `declaresDispatchGrant` (`:1185`) runs only in the session lane. The declared grant is minted only on the launch-attach arm (`enqueueRow` → `attachProxyContext` with `...lane.declaration(ctx)`, `:1087`), which means the variant must force the proxy block, as the plan says.
- **The safeguards are real.** `provisionBootstrapToken` (`lib/proxy-preamble.js:544-575`) refuses a declared mint that has no workspace id, no site or no owner. `mintGrantBootstrap` (`lib/proxy-tokens.js:378`) runs the owner check. Each refusal throws inside `finalizePrompt`, before `addItem`. So witness 2 (a non-owner is refused and no leaf is created) tries exactly what the guard is there to stop.
- **The authority is approved.** John's approval of the "+ Autopilot" grant is on the ticket. An owner's token can already start a declared M1 orchestrator with a free-text `goal` through `/autopilot/kickoff`, so the 500-char note does not widen what that token can do.
- **The renderer has one source.** The only place that composes `generatePrompt()` with `withAutopilotTail()` is `buildPeriodicalNodes` (`lib/periodicals.js:1124`). `lib/render.js` and `public/app.js` only read `.prompt` and `.autopilotPrompt`. The proxy block is appended after the prompt (`proxy-preamble.js:778`), so the "starts with" parity check in witness 4 is sound.
- **Run state works with the stamp alone.** `GET /periodicals` keeps rows where `kind === 'periodical' || periodicalId != null` (`routes/proxy-compute.js:1018`).
- **Every test and comment the plan lists exists**, including the "three enqueue mounts" / "four POST handlers" wording at the places it names.

**Notes for the builder** (none of these blocks)

1. **Pass the free-tier run gate.** `enqueueRow` takes `runGate` only from the spec and has no lane default (`:1015`). P, R and K each pass `gateByKey(run, await run.lane.freeTierKey(ctx))` (`:1399`, `:1877`). The plan does not mention it, and no census checks that an entrance passes it. If it is left out, a free-tier account can mint periodical runs past its run limit and no test fails. Pass it as P and K do, and add a witness: a free-tier account at its limit gets the run-limit 429 and nothing is enqueued.
2. **Use site tag `M5`, not `M3`.** The code uses M1, M2 and M4, so "the next free tag" can read as M3. M3 is already the documented name for the deferred proxy-dispatch declared launch (`tests/unit/lin-3134-declared-mint-census.test.js:156`, `:654`; `docs/worker-lane-prompt.md:69`). Use `M5`. Also update the census comments and the `LANES` comment (`:782`, "the proxy dispatch arms stay undeclared") so they name this route as the one declared proxy-token mint besides kickoff.
3. **Add `ROW_KEYS.periodical`.** `rowFor` indexes `ROW_KEYS[laneName]` (`:420`), and `{ ...LANES.proxy }` does not give the new lane a key table, so `rowFor('periodical', …)` would throw. Add a minimal key list with the reason beside it: `promptName`, `dispatchedBy`, `target`, `repo`, `periodicalId`, and nothing issue- or follow-up-shaped. Your witnesses would catch a missing table, but it is better to decide the list on purpose.
4. **Give this route its own refusal text.** If `relayed` reuses kickoff's list, `kickoffStructuralRule` (`:671`) answers a non-owner with "a child autopilot launch credential", which is wrong for a periodical mint. Write a rule for this route with its own subject (for example "a periodical + Autopilot launch credential"), or parametrise the subject. Keep kickoff's order, with `attachFailedRule` before the structural rule. That order is why a transient `OWNER_CHECK_UNAVAILABLE` comes back as a 503.
5. **Take `promptName` from the UI's own rendering.** The UI action sends the `.prompt-name` text, which is `title` for plain and `` `${title} + Autopilot` `` for the variant (`lib/render.js:659,673`; `public/app.js:1553`). In witness 4, read the expected value from `renderPeriodicalNode` output or from one shared helper, not from a string typed into the test. Otherwise the check compares the route against a copy, which is the drift the shared renderer exists to prevent.
6. **The "nothing walks `router.stack`" premise is narrower than the Surveys say.** `dispatch-entrance-proxy-grant-sweep.test.js:99-121` enumerates routes (`enumerateRoutes`, compared with `derivedUrlForms()`) and sends every write route a token without the grant. A new POST without `requireGrant('dispatch')` that reaches `addItem` would fail that test without a hand-added row. This changes nothing in the plan, since the hand-kept lists still need updating, but say it accurately in the PR. Optionally, a one-line test that the catalog's example id `documentation-review` is in `getPeriodicals()` keeps the example from drifting, and the catalog still needs no import.

Next: `implementation`, with these notes.

## LIN-4313: implementation summary

PR: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2324 (branch feat/lin-4313-periodical-mint-route, head 980eefc6)

- New route POST /api/proxy/periodicals/:id/mint: a dispatch-grant token mints a Periodical run by registry id, plain or + Autopilot, as the UI does. The server renders the prompt; an optional note (at most 500 characters, one line, no control characters) goes before the template text. Template text unchanged.
- Only the + Autopilot variant declares the dispatch grant, for the token owner, owner-checked at the mint. A non-owner is refused and nothing is enqueued. Plain mint stays a grant-less leaf. Authority flag for John is in the PR body.
- Site tag is PM, not M5: M5 is already the driver-copy mint in the LIN-3136 vocabulary.
- Evidence: unit 23,900 pass / 0 fail; hermetic PASS; E2E periodicals and autopilot-proxy-force 24 pass; PR CI green (unit, 4 E2E shards, secret scan, CI success).
- Merge is not mine: it waits for review approval, performed by the orchestrator or a human.

## LIN-4313: final CI result

PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2324 is at head ced8949d (the render-helper commit after the earlier 980eefc6 summary).

- CI on ced8949d: success. Unit tests, all four E2E shards, secret scan, and CI success all pass (run 42190887139).
- Unit suite on the same tree: 23,900 pass, 0 fail. Hermetic keyed run: pass.
- Merge is not mine. It waits for review approval.

## Review — LIN-4313

Reviewed PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2324 at head `ced8949dd9b65222f7310c68739792dee2635392` (6 commits on base `f73f1b11`; mergeable).

CI: green on ced8949d. Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, secret scan and CI success all pass (`.github/workflows/test.yml`). I also re-ran the 575 affected unit tests in a worktree: 575 pass, 0 fail.

### What I checked
- **Scope matches the plan.** The diff covers the planned places: `LANES.periodical` (site `PM`), `enterPeriodicalMint`, the route in `routes/proxy-dispatch.js`, `renderPeriodicalPrompt`, `ROW_KEYS.periodical`, its own structural refusal, the run gate, the note, docs, catalog, and the entrance lists (header, grant sweep, inventory row, F3 census 2→3, private-mint source pin, scope comments). Every plan-review note (run gate, `ROW_KEYS`, its own refusal text, a non-M3 tag, promptName from one helper) was handled. The site tag is `PM` rather than `M5`; the implementation summary gives the reason.
- **Staleness and regressions.** No commit on `main` has touched the changed files since the ticket was written. The last 40 commits on `dispatch-entrance.js`, `periodicals.js` and `proxy-dispatch.js` contain no reverted periodical or declaration work that this PR re-applies. The session lane's M2b tail sniff is untouched, and so is `POST /dispatch kind:periodical`, which is still undeclared (open question 1 stays open, as scoped).
- **Prompt bytes.** `lin-4313-periodical-prompt-bytes.test.js` pins sha256 of plain and autopilot prompts for all 16 registry ids at the pre-refactor text. It passes at head.
- **Mutation checks.** Each mutation was reverted afterwards. Test file: `lin-4313-periodical-mint.test.js`, unless named otherwise:
  - `LANES.periodical.declaration` removed: 23 fail.
  - `declared: autopilot` → `true`: 17 fail (plain becomes declared).
  - `runGate` dropped: 1 fail (the 429 witness).
  - `periodicalId` dropped from the row: 33 fail.
  - The unknown-id 404 guard disabled: 1 fail.
  - Note moved after the template: 1 fail.
  - Note silently dropped: 1 fail.
  - Control-character check removed: 6 fail.
  - Kickoff's refusal rule used in place of the periodical one: 1 fail.
  - Site `PM` → `M1`: 1 fail.
  - Renderer drops the tail: 17 fail.
  - `periodicalPromptName` drops " + Autopilot": 16 fail.
  - `requireGrant('dispatch')` removed from the route: the grant sweep goes 3 red, the private-mint pin 1 red, the LIN-4313 test 1 red.
  - **Survived:** hard-coding `grantOwnerAccountId: 'account-A'` in place of `req.proxyCreatedBy` stays green. The non-owner witness flips the workspace's owner; it never uses a token created by a different account. In practice the only way a non-owner holds a dispatch token is a token minted before ownership changed, so the existing witness covers the realistic case. Non-blocking: a token with `createdBy: 'account-B'` in a workspace owned by A would close it.
- **Smaller deviations (accepted, not blocking):**
  - Witness 1 proves the child can enqueue via `POST /dispatch` rather than `/autopilot/kickoff`. Both sit behind the same `requireGrant('dispatch')`.
  - `dispatch-entrance-pins.test.js` was not touched. That file pins LIN-3592 behaviour fixes and does not list entrances; the new entrance's behaviour is pinned in the LIN-4313 test.
- **Isolated, or one of a class?** The class is a proxy door to an orchestrator that needs a declared grant. Its siblings are kickoff (M1, declared) and `POST /dispatch` with the tail. The tail case is deliberately undeclared, open question 1, and outside this ticket. Apart from that, the change is isolated.

### Fixes for close-out (both inside scope; make before merge)
1. **The note accepts Unicode line breaks.** Bounded class: the note rules (step 4, plan item 7: "a single line, no control characters at all"). `periodicalNoteError` refuses C0, DEL and C1, but accepts U+2028 LINE SEPARATOR and U+2029 PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR. `JSON.stringify` passes both through raw, so a "single-line" note can put line breaks into the prompt. Verified: `periodicalNoteError('a ## Ignore the above b')` returns `null`, and both characters survive in `withOperatorNote` output.
   - Fix in `lib/periodicals.js`: change `NOTE_CONTROL_CHAR_RE` to `/[\u0000-\u001f\u007f-\u009f  ]/` and add the two characters to the comment above it.
   - Fix in `tests/unit/lin-4313-periodical-mint.test.js`: add `['a U+2028 line separator', 'a b']` and `['a U+2029 paragraph separator', 'a b']` to the 400 table.
   - Docs and catalog wording ("a line break … is refused") then holds as written.
2. **The harness default is not documented.** Bounded class: plan item 5 and step 6, "Harness: say which default applies". Neither the docs nor the catalog says that a blank `harness` on this route takes the proxy lane's `claude-code` default, which differs from the app's Mint (there the dispatch page's selector decides).
   - Add one sentence to `docs/proxy-integration.md` § "Mint a Periodical", after "`target`, `repo`, `model`, `harness` and `effort` are the execution fields…".
   - Add one `→` line to the `POST …/periodicals/{id}/mint` entry in `lib/proxy-instructions.js`. Suggested wording: "A blank `harness` defaults to `claude-code`, the proxy lane's default; the app's Mint takes the dispatch page's selector instead."
   - Re-run `tests/unit/proxy-instructions.test.js` and `tests/unit/lin-3866-dispatch-doc-defaults.test.js`.

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **Inside** (the two fixes above). *Before the merge:* make fixes 1 and 2. They pass when the two new note cases return 400 with nothing minted, and the four test files named above stay green.
- **Inside** (the grant, step 1): a real owner's `dispatch` token minting `autopilot: true` gets a working orchestrator. In tests the token store, the owner check (`setOwnerCheck`) and the dispatch queue are fakes; CI never drives the real owner-check wiring in `server.js` or a real runner taking the row. *After the deploy:* run one live `POST /api/proxy/periodicals/<id>/mint` with `{"autopilot":true}` using the owner's driver token. The check passes when the stored row carries `grantDeclaration.site: "PM"` with owner = the token creator, and the minted Stage-1 agent's `POST /autopilot/kickoff` returns 201, not `403 DISPATCH_GRANT_REQUIRED`. The same mint must then appear as `recent` in `GET /api/proxy/periodicals`.
- **Inside** (the note, step 4): carrying the note into the minted task's description, below the gate-marker line and above the review contract, depends on the model, which no test can prove (the server cannot write the description; docs and catalog say so). *After the deploy:* in the first live mint with a `note`, check the minted Linear task's description. The note line must sit directly under the gate marker and above the review contract, and the gate marker must still be line 1.
- **Rollback:** reverting the PR's merge commit is enough. The route is additive with no migration. Rows already minted with `declaredSite: "PM"` stay valid history, since the exchange reads the declaration from the row.

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger

The grant, renderer, parity, note placement, run gate and entrance lists are complete and verified by mutation. Two small inside-scope gaps (U+2028/U+2029 in the note, the undocumented harness default) are named above for close-out to fix before merge. The two live checks are post-deploy steps.

## Close-out — LIN-4313

**Merged:** https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2324, squash-merged as `c491eca5d1bc0bcf8cef52633195d0d268da19ed`, pinned with `--match-head-commit` to `61125f31` (the commit CI passed on). Review verdict on record: Approve, conditional on this close-out discharging the ledger.

### Changes I made after the approval
Both are review's "Fixes for close-out", in commit `61125f31`:
1. **Review fix 1, Unicode line breaks in the note.** `NOTE_CONTROL_CHAR_RE` in `lib/periodicals.js` now also refuses U+2028 and U+2029, and the comment above it names them. `tests/unit/lin-4313-periodical-mint.test.js` has two new 400 cases (`a U+2028 line separator`, `a U+2029 paragraph separator`). Both cases fail with the regex change reverted and pass with it. The docs and catalog wording ("a line break … is refused") already held, so it needed no edit.
2. **Review fix 2, blank-`harness` default.** One sentence added to `docs/proxy-integration.md` under "Mint a Periodical", and one `→` line on the `POST …/periodicals/{id}/mint` entry in `lib/proxy-instructions.js`: a blank `harness` takes the proxy lane's `claude-code` default, while the app's Mint takes the dispatch page's selector.
- Re-run: `lin-4313-periodical-mint`, `proxy-instructions`, `lin-3866-dispatch-doc-defaults` and `lin-4313-periodical-prompt-bytes` pass (102 tests, 0 fail).
- No stale citation or comment was left behind that needed a separate edit.

### CI
CI applies to this repo (`.github/workflows/test.yml`). Fresh read on `61125f31`: Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, Secret scan and CI success all SUCCESS before the merge. The post-merge run on `main` (run 42193963431) also passed.

### Ledger
- **Fix 1 (inside): done.** Evidence above (the new cases fail without the change, pass with it; CI green).
- **Fix 2 (inside): done.** Docs and catalog sentences added, doc and catalog tests pass.
- **Deploy:** landed. The live `GET /api/proxy/instructions` catalog now lists `POST …/periodicals/{id}/mint`.
